steps: Start by cooking the quinoa so that it cools while you prep everything else. Combine quinoa and stock and bring to a boil. Put a lid on, turn the heat down to very low and leave for 15 minutes.
To make the herby sauce, combine all its ingredients and whiz together with a stick blender.
Sauté the shallots in olive oil for 7 minutes until soft and lightly browned.

Slice the asparagus and broccolini in half on a diagonal and slice the broccolini again in half lengthways. Bring a pot of well salted water to a boil. Turn down to a simmer and blanch the broccolini and asparagus for 2 1/2 minutes or until just tender. Defrost the frozen peas.
Pan fry the haloumi in olive oil until golden brown. Toast the slithered almonds in a dry pan until lightly browned.
Assemble the salad by combining quinoa, veggies, shallots, 3/4 of the slithered almonds, haloumi, mint, parsley, dill, juice of 1 lemon, olive oil and a pinch of chilli flakes. Toss to combine.
Spread the herby tahini sauce on a serving dish and top with the salad and the remaining slithered almonds.
recipes.title: Green Spring Quinoa Salad with Halloumi and Herby Tahini

recipes.notes: Any large pot that goes from stovetop to oven with a fitting lid works; a Dutch oven is perfect. Rice still firm: lid back on with a small splash of stock or water for a few more minutes. Tastes flat: one more pinch of salt or squeeze of lime. Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for a few days; reheat covered with a splash of water or stock.
steps: Preheat the oven to {{425F}}. Season the chicken thighs well on both sides with salt and pepper.
Sear the chicken: heat the avocado oil in a large oven-safe pot with a lid. Sear the thighs on both sides until golden, then take them out and set them aside on a plate.
Sauté the onion: add the chopped onion to the same pot, season with salt and pepper and sauté until it's soft and lightly golden.
Add the aromatics and spices: stir in the grated ginger, grated garlic, garam masala, cumin and turmeric (plus the chili, if you're using it). Sauté for a minute to release all that flavor.
Stir in the chopped cilantro stems. Save the leaves for the end.
Rinse the basmati rice well, then add it to the pot and stir so every grain gets coated in the onion and spice mixture.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken stock. Scrape up all the bits stuck to the bottom of the pot, then season with another pinch of salt.
Nestle the chicken back into the pot skin side up, cover with the lid and roast for 30 minutes.
Uncover and roast for another 10 minutes so the skin gets its color back.
Finish and serve: take the pot out of the oven, zest the lime over the top, squeeze over the juice and shower everything with the cilantro leaves. Serve straight from the pot.
recipes.title: One-Pot Coconut Chicken and Rice

recipes.notes: Squeeze the grated cucumbers well, or the tzatziki turns watery. The tzatziki and the beef filling can both be made ahead and kept covered in the fridge; keep the chopped salad undressed until right before serving. Best fresh out of the pan, so sear only what you're eating.
steps: Prep the pitas: slice each of the two pitas around the edges so that you have two flat pieces. Set them aside while you make everything else.

Mix the filling: in a bowl, combine the ground beef, finely chopped red onion, grated garlic, dried oregano and paprika. Season generously with kosher salt and cracked black pepper, then bring it all together until everything is evenly mixed.
Spread and press the beef mixture onto the inside part of each pita half. It should be spread all the way to the edges. The meat will shrink while it cooks.

Make the tzatziki: grate the Persian cucumbers and squeeze out as much juice as you can. Add them to a bowl with the full-fat Greek yogurt, garlic, lemon juice and chopped dill. Season well with kosher salt and stir.
Chop the salad: finely chop the tomato, Persian cucumbers and red onion. Toss with olive oil, red wine vin and season with salt.

Sear the pitas: in a hot pan with a little drizzle of olive oil, place the arayes meat side down and sear until the meat is golden and crisp, around 2 min, then flip over and toast a couple more minutes on the pita side.
Pile it on: top each hot pita with the chopped salad, a big spoonful of tzatziki and plenty of fresh dill. Sprinkle over some dried oregano and eat right away, while the bread is still crunchy.
recipes.title: Greek-Inspired Cheat Arayes with Dill Tzatziki

steps: Backofen auf {{220C}} Ober-/Unterhitze vorheizen. Auberginenscheiben auf Küchenkrepp auslegen & salzen, ca. 15 min ziehen lassen, mit Zewa abtupfen, wenden und den Vorgang wiederholen. Mit Olivenöl, Kreuzkümmel, Salz, Sumach und etwas Pfeffer einreiben. Auf ein Blech legen und 35-45 Minuten rösten, bis sie weich und an den Rändern crispy sind.
Joghurt, Tahini, Zitronensaft, Knoblauch und Salz verrühren. Optional 1-2 EL kaltes Wasser dazu.

Kichererbsen abseihen. Schalotten in einer Pfanne in etwas Öl anrösten. Butter dazugeben und bei mittlerer Hitze schmelzen. Paprikamark dazugeben und etwa 1-2 Minuten anrösten. Pul Biber, Kreuzkümmel und Paprikapulver dazugeben und kurz ziehen lassen. Kichererbsen dazu und 3-5 Minuten in der Paprika-Butter schwenken. Mit Salz, optional mehr Butter und nem Spritzer Zitronensaft abschmecken.

Tahini-Joghurt großzügig auf Tellern verstreichen. Die Auberginen und die warmen Kichererbsen samt der Butter aus der Pfanne darauf verteilen. Mit Granatapfelkernen oder Pickled Onions und Petersilie garnieren. Zum Schluss mit etwas Sumach bestreuen und mit gutem Olivenöl und noch mehr Tahini beträufeln. Mit warmem Fladenbrot servieren.

steps: Preheat the oven to {{220C}} top/bottom heat. Lay the eggplant slices out on paper towels & salt them, let them sit for approx. 15 min, blot with paper towel, turn them over and repeat the process. Rub with olive oil, cumin, salt, sumac and a little pepper. Place on a baking sheet and roast for 35-45 minutes, until soft and crispy at the edges.
Stir together the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt. Optionally add 1-2 tbsp cold water.

Drain the chickpeas. Sauté the shallots in a pan in a little oil. Add the butter and melt it over medium heat. Add the tomato paste and sauté for about 1-2 minutes. Add the Aleppo pepper, cumin and paprika powder and let them infuse briefly. Add the chickpeas and toss them in the paprika butter for 3-5 minutes. Season with salt, optionally more butter and a squeeze of lemon juice.

Spread the tahini yogurt generously on plates. Distribute the eggplants and the warm chickpeas, along with the butter from the pan, on top. Garnish with pomegranate seeds or pickled onions and parsley. Finally sprinkle with a little sumac and drizzle with good olive oil and even more tahini. Serve with warm flatbread.

steps: Mix everything together, then leave it for 10 minutes. This is the important bit: the chia, flax and psyllium turn into a gel, which binds the seeds and makes it much easier to spread. If you don’t have psyllium, just add a bit more milled flax.
Spread it thinly over a lined baking tray and bake at {{150C}} for 40 minutes. Let it cool, then break it into shards.

steps: Heat the oven to {{325F}}. Season the chuck roast generously with salt and the 1 tbsp black pepper, rubbing it evenly over the meat.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the meat on all sides until browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Set it aside.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the onions over medium heat and sauté until golden brown and translucent, about 6-8 minutes.
Deglaze the pan with ¼ cup of the red wine, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom. Keep cooking until the liquid has evaporated and the onions are deep burgundy.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for two minutes. Add the broth, the remaining wine, rosemary, thyme, bay leaves, garlic and 1 tsp salt.
Return the meat to the pot and bring to a simmer. Cover and move to the oven for 2 hours.

Take the pot out and set the garlic aside. Add the potatoes and carrots, pushing them to the bottom. Squeeze the garlic into the broth and stir, then stack the meat on top of the vegetables so its top is exposed.
Return to the oven uncovered for 45 minutes.
Lift out the meat and shred it. Discard the herbs. Whisk 2-3 tbsp of the broth with the 1 tbsp flour in a small bowl until smooth.
Pour the slurry into the pot and simmer 2-3 minutes until thickened. Return the meat, mix well and serve.
recipes.title: Pot Roast

ingredients.name: bone in skin on chicken thighs and/or drumsticks

steps: Heat the oven to {{350F}}. Put the chicken in a roasting dish and season with the salt, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, oregano and black pepper. Drizzle with olive oil and toss until evenly coated.
Add the onions and thyme, then pour the bone broth into the pan, not directly over the chicken, so the seasoning stays on.
Cover and bake for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Take the chicken out and raise the oven to {{450F}}.
Discard the thyme sprigs, then move the chicken to a clean plate.
Whisk ¼ cup of the pan broth with the 2 tbsp arrowroot until smooth. Whisk this slurry into the rest of the broth, return the chicken and toss to coat in the sauce.
Return to the oven uncovered for 20 minutes longer, basting every 5 minutes (optional), until golden brown and the gravy has thickened.
Serve over rice.
recipes.title: Braised Chicken with Bone Broth Gravy

steps: Cover the pumpkin seeds with water and soak for at least 6 to 8 hours. Drain, rinse and pat dry on a clean kitchen towel.
Heat the oven to {{325F}}. Spread the seeds over a large tray and roast for 15 minutes, stirring halfway through. Cool for about 5 minutes.

Pulse the seeds a few times in a food processor to break them into a crumble, then run it continuously, scraping down the sides now and then. They go from crumble to a thick dry paste and then loosen into a smooth, runny butter in about 15-18 minutes.
Add the salt and blend again to mix it in; add more salt if you like. Store in an airtight jar or container.
Warm a tsp of oil and agave syrup in a small non-stick pan. Add the figs cut side down and cook undisturbed for about 3 minutes. Flip and cook 3 minutes more, then take off the heat.
Toast the bread, spread with pumpkin seed butter, top with the caramelized figs and finish with a pinch of salt and/or a drizzle of agave syrup.
